summary: Mery Cecconi is an Indologist. She has been a PhD candidate at Leiden University, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Mette Halskov Hansen is a scholar of Sinology. After completing an MPhil at the University of Oslo (2020–2022) and serving as a research assistant at Aarhus University (2022–2023), she became a professor at the University of Oslo (attested 2026).

Michael Alram is a historian and numismatist of Indology and Iranian-Central Asian studies. He studied under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer at the University of Vienna, later serving as director of the Münzkabinett (2008–2020) and vice-president of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2013–2022).

Michael Aris was a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. He held posts at St Antony's College and Oxford University (~1989–1999) and Harvard University (~1992–1993).

Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and served as a Central Asia Specialist at the Royal Library of Berlin from 1988 to 2019.

Michael Baumgarten was a religious studies scholar who studied in Berlin under Franz Bopp and at Kiel University. He worked at Kiel University (~1839–1846) and served as Professor of Theology at the University of Rostock from 1850 to 1858.

Michael Baxandall was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Munich, and Pavia. He held positions at the Warburg Institute, the Courtauld Institute of Art (~1982–1986), the University of California, Berkeley (1987), and Cornell University (~1989–1995).

Michael Bernays studied at the universities of Bonn and Heidelberg, where he studied under Adolf Holtzmann. He later held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael Brattus Jones is an Indologist and historian. Attested as a retired Professor of History at the University of Delhi in 2011, he pursued a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011–2016).
Michael Brunner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied for a Bachelor of Arts at the University of Michigan (2024–2026). He became Abbot at One River Zen in 2021.

Michael C. Shapiro is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He pursued his career at the University of Washington, where he became Professor around 1970 and later Professor Emeritus of Hindi (attested 2026).

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and anthropology. Educated at Wesleyan and Oxford, he taught at Oxford and the London School of Economics before joining Durham University, where he became Professor of Anthropology in 1992.

Michael Comans is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati and Jan Willem de Jong, completing his studies at the Australian National University (~1983–1987). He later served on the faculty at the University of Sydney (~1989–2004).
Michael J. Conway is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He serves as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and is a faculty member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Michael Coulson was an Indologist and linguist who completed his BA and DPhil at the University of Oxford. From around 1964 to 1975, he served as Lecturer and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Edinburgh.

Michael Eido Luetchford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford (~1963–1967) and studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima from ~1974 to 2007.

Michael Fertig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Würzburg under Othmar Frank. He taught Latin at the University of Passau in 1846 and was Rector of the Hans-Carossa-Gymnasium Landshut from 1855 to 1869.

Michael Friedrich is a Sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich (~1974–1984), where he also worked as an assistant. He served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

Michael G. Morony is a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (BA) and UCLA (MA), and was appointed Professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1974.
